title: The kind acceptance harness and an honest capability matrix
request: Each kind is called supported only when it reaches a careful data scientist's decisions on a synthetic replica of a realistic case; the Domain packs page must show that, generated, not hand-written maturity labels.
spec: Each kind ships a replica generator and an acceptance test; make kinds-check runs them all; the Domain packs page and /api/kinds show a capability matrix generated from the results (supported only when the acceptance passes, otherwise partial with what is missing). Done when the matrix is generated, the existing kinds pass, and a failing acceptance turns its row from supported to partial in a test.
plan: Give the interface two hooks: case(seed) (the replica as a person brings it) and accept(run) (the decisions, each checked on the finished stage records).

Write a harness that builds the project the way a person would: attach the data and the label file, accept the agent's proposal, write the prediction moment, tick the columns the moment's own words name as written later.
Use the existing replicas (fraud, tickets, delivery) and write two new ones in dclab_core: subscription churn (binary) and product reviews (text), each with its traps.
Store the results with make kinds-check; build the matrix from the file; label the packs from the matrix and remove the hand-written labels.
Test the matrix logic (a failure turns a row partial, a forged 'supported' with a failing check is partial, a never-run kind is partial) and that the committed file matches a fresh run.

decisions.decision: Decisions are checked on the engine's own records (roles of columns, the split description, the metric, the holdout against the stage's baselines), never on a separate computation.
decisions.why: The acceptance must judge what DCLab decided, not what a test recomputes.

decisions.decision: Thresholds are principled margins (0.1 above chance or the majority, MAE at most 0.9 times the median's) rather than fitted to the first run.
decisions.why: A threshold tuned to the run passes by construction and says nothing.

decisions.decision: The matrix trusts no stored 'supported': it recounts the checks.
decisions.why: A result file edited by hand or a partial failure must never show as supported.

decisions.decision: The fraud case runs on the full engine (not quick), in its own test file.
decisions.why: Quick mode samples 3000 rows and leaves too few frauds; its own file lets the parallel runner start it first.

change: dclab_rnd/kinds/acceptance.py (Case, Run, check, kept_out, build, run, run_all, write, load, matrix), kinds/__main__.py and make kinds-check, case() and accept() on the five kinds, replicas subscription_churn and product_reviews, generated kinds/capability.json, /api/kinds with the matrix, draft/pack.cards labelling packs Supported, Partial or Not built from the matrix, the leakage reviewer's moment rule reading 'come later', tests for acceptance and the matrix.

findings.defect: On the ticket replica, first_response_minutes stayed a model feature although it is known only after the queue answers.
findings.scenario: The person wrote the moment 'When the ticket is created, before anyone reads it; the agent who closes it and the first response time come later.' The audit flagged resolved_by (a near copy of the label) but not first_response_minutes, whose name and signal look harmless; the multiclass kind was partial.
findings.cause: The leakage reviewer's moment rule recognised only clauses with 'excluded', 'not known', 'unavailable' and similar, not 'come later'.
findings.fix: The moment rule now also reads 'come(s) later', 'known later', 'written later', 'recorded later', 'afterwards', with those words kept out of the column-matching stems.
findings.test: The multiclass acceptance (first_response_minutes kept out) and the leakage reviewer's tests.

findings.defect: The harness could not attach the fraud replica's label file.
findings.scenario: Both files were written to the data folder before attaching the rides; attaching the data clears the folder, so the label file was gone.
findings.cause: attach_data keeps only the data file it registers.
findings.fix: The harness writes the label file again after attaching the data.

findings.defect: The challenge-mode privacy test failed by chance.
findings.scenario: A six-digit order id appeared inside a random salted hash in the service's model.pkl ('h:901433f9...'): the search for row values in the deliverables found it.
findings.cause: Hex hashes made with a random key can contain any short digit string.
findings.fix: The test removes the one-way salted hash tokens (h: and 16 hex digits) before searching for row values; every real value is still searched.

findings.defect: A forbidden text column still reached the model, and the text acceptance could not see it.
findings.scenario: The proposal forbade review_text as 'identifier-like (100% unique)' and also proposed it as the text column; its role was 'blocked', yet the TF-IDF recipe on review_text was chosen. Made worse on purpose (shop_reply as free text carrying the label, review_text carrying nothing), all six decisions still passed with holdout AUC 1.0.
findings.cause: The kind's text columns did not drop forbidden ones; the text recipe builds documents from every declared text column; kept_out read only the role; the 'text is modelled' check read the solution, not what was modelled; free text was flagged as an identifier.
findings.fix: A forbidden column is never modelled as text; free text is no longer flagged as an identifier when uniqueness is its only signal; kept_out requires the role blocked (or identifier where allowed) and the column absent from the modelled text; the text check reads the role 'text' and the data stage's text columns; a 'no copy of the label' bound (AUC below 0.99) was added, and the replica's words made noisier so an honest model lands near 0.9.

findings.defect: Two leak decisions passed because the harness ticked what the product leaves to the person, and one passed for the wrong reason.
findings.scenario: The harness ticked every moment-rule proposal, though the product shows them unticked; the case moments were written to name the leaks. With a neutral moment the multiclass kind turned partial; delivered_at 'passed' only because it was a second date column set aside, not because it was blocked.
findings.cause: The simulated person did more than the product offers, and kept_out accepted any non-feature role.
findings.fix: The person adopts the plan beside the proposal (the adopt_plan move the product offers): its forbidden columns and the ones it keeps out until confirmed; moments are neutral; leak checks require the role blocked.
findings.test: Multiclass and regression acceptances with neutral moments.

findings.defect: The broadened moment rule named unrelated columns.
findings.scenario: 'When the order is placed: the basket value and the price are known, and the delivery time comes later.' flagged order_time, basket_value and price, because the whole sentence was one clause and 'time' matched order_time.
findings.cause: Clauses were split only at full stops, semicolons and but/while; a generic word could name a column alone.
findings.fix: Clauses also split at a colon and at ', and the/a/its…' (a list after 'exclude' stays one clause); generic stems (time, date, value, price, count…) never name a column alone.

findings.defect: Running the acceptance directly could send stage records to a configured live model.
findings.scenario: python -m dclab_rnd.kinds without DCLAB_NO_LIVE_MODELS: the critic was mocked, but the stage notes (narrate, explain_stage) still went through the gateway.
findings.cause: Only one model path was switched off.
findings.fix: The stages run inside the gateway's private scope, where no purpose is offered a model.

findings.defect: Missing tests for the declared baselines, the unstratified group split and the matrix routes; one binary decision could never fail.
findings.scenario: 'The data stage says accuracy flatters' checked a sentence the binary kind always writes.
findings.cause: Checks written for coverage, not for what can go wrong.
findings.fix: The harness checks every kind's declared baselines against the final stage's; tests for stratify=False on a classification keeping both classes, /api/kinds' matrix and note, /api/packs labels; the binary check replaced by the leakage audit's measured inflation (above 0.1); the rare-event kind checks the label join is on the order.

measurements.name: kind acceptance on replicas
measurements.gate: Each decision of each kind holds on its replica (fixed with the kind before its first run): rare event 7 decisions, text 6, binary 6, multiclass 6, regression 5.
measurements.result: After the review: all five supported under stricter decisions (rare event 9/9, text 8/8, binary 7/7, multiclass 7/7, regression 6/6). Text holdout AUC 0.87-0.91 over three seeds after the replica was made honest; before, 0.99.
measurements.next: Every new kind (16.3 onward) ships its case and decisions; the matrix shows it partial until they hold.

outcome: Done: make kinds-check, a generated capability matrix in /api/kinds and on the Domain packs page, all five kinds supported; one real leakage gap found by the first run and fixed in the product.
lessons: An acceptance on a replica found a real gap the unit tests never saw: a post-moment column with a harmless name.
A test that searches artefacts for data values must exclude one-way hashes, or it fails by chance.
A simulated person in an acceptance harness must do only what the product offers, or the acceptance measures the harness.
Every acceptance check should be able to fail: a check that reads a sentence the code always writes measures nothing.
A replica that is too easy (AUC 0.99) cannot tell a leak from skill: tune it to land where an honest model would.
